Cs No. 14758/2016 Cnr No. Dlct01-002086 2014 Bhartiya Parivardhan Sanstha, (through its General Secretary Sh Dinesh Kumar), D-1, Basti Vikas Kendra, Nand Nagri, Delhi-110093. ............Plai Versus 1. texts.facts: The present suit has been filed by the plaintiff seeking recovery of Rs. 20,00,000/-/- along with pendente-lite interest pleading inter-alia as under:- i. That the plaintiff is a Registered Society under the Societies Registration Act, and is working for Up-liftment and Development of Children, Women and Rehabilitation of Drug Addicts and is having its registered office at D-1, Basti Vikas Kendra, Nand Nagri, Delhi-110093 and the present suit is being filed through its General Secretary Bhartiya Parivardhan Sanstha vs Department Of Social Welfare on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51433371/ 1 Shri Dinesh Kumar. ii. That the plaintiff was awarded a work order/contract by the Department of Social Welfare Govt. of NCT of Delhi i.e. the defendant No.1 to set up a drug de-addiction centre at the Beggar Home Complex at Lampur, Delhi in the year 2010 initially for a period of one year which was subsequently extended from time to time and was last extended till December 2012. iii. That initially the contract was only for 20 inmates per month and the Department of Finance Govt. of NCT of Delhi i.e, defendant No.2 had concurred the expenditure of Rs. 25 lakhs (Rs.23 lakhs in respect of recurring expenses and Rs.2 lakhs in respect of non-recurring expenses) CS No 14758/16 Bhartiya Parivardhan Sanstha Vs Department of Social Welfare Page No 2/44 for a period of one year in accordance with the details of the proposal submitted by the plaintiff to the Department of Social Welfare, Govt. of NCT of Delhi i.e. defendant no.1. The department had also reserved its right to terminate the said work order after giving 30 days notice without assigning any reason. iv. That the plaintiff was also given right to terminate/windup services at Lampur after giving 30 days advance notice to the department. The plaintiff was also bound to comply with the prescribed standard of services and manpower requirement. The work order for the running drug de-addiction services could be extended beyond a period of one year on the basis evaluation by a Monitoring committee and on the basis satisfactory performance of the plaintiff. v. That the department under the work order was to provide free of cost building space, electricity, security, water facility to the plaintiff for setting up the drug de-addiction centre. vi. That the plaintiff was also responsible for the safety and well being of the inmates under their charge in the said drug de-addiction centre. vii. That as per the plaintiff the defendant did not adhere to their contract for the upkeep of only 20 inmates per month and kept on putting burden CS No 14758/16 Bhartiya Parivardhan Sanstha Vs Department of Social Welfare Page No 3/44 for the upkeep of more than 20 inmates per month on the plaintiff which arose to an alarming strength in certain months thereby putting enormous financial pressure on the plaintiff. viii. That the plaintiff on a number of occasions had written letters to the Department of Social Welfare for providing security and other manpower which was essential for the upkeep and maintenance of the inmates exceeding 20 i.e. the sanctioned strength. The behavior and pattern of the inmates remained volatile and violent all the time during their rehabilitation programme and to control them it was essential Bhartiya Parivardhan Sanstha vs Department Of Social Welfare on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51433371/ 2 to have more manpower in the proportion of the manpower meant for 20 inmate as assigned in the work order meaning thereby more manpower was required for the inmates exceeding 20 inmates. ix. That the department i.e. defendant No.2 did not provide any security or manpower to the plaintiff when it was burdened with more inmates exceeding number 20 i.e. the sanctioned strength however, the department had given permission to the plaintiff to employ more manpower for the running of the drug de-addiction centre at Lampur in absence of the more manpower as provided by the department. But the department did not pay CS No 14758/16 Bhartiya Parivardhan Sanstha Vs Department of Social Welfare Page No 4/44 anything or rather curtailed its expenditure on the manpower so employed for the control of the inmates exceeding number 20. x. That strength of de-addiction centre at Lampur run by the plaintiff had gone beyond the sanctioned capacity of 20 inmates since March 2012 and additional funds were required for catering to the needs of additional inmates and the plaintiff had been regularly sending letters seeking additional funds for additional inmates. xi. That the Department of Social Welfare on the basis of the total approved recurring cost of Rs.23 lakhs for 12 months for 20 inmates per day have calculated an expenditure per inmate per day as Rs.319/- for the additional inmates and on that basis had calculated the expenditure incurred by the plaintiff on the additional inmates per day. xii. That the plaintiff has been provided recurring funds for inmates per day and when the inmates strength increases correspondingly the plaintiff had to make arrangements for their food, medicines, beddings and additional staff and had claimed additional expenditure of Rs.325/- per day per inmate for additional inmates. xiii. That the strength of the inmates of the de-addiction centre at Lampur run by the plaintiff has been regularly monitored, checked and verified CS No 14758/16 Bhartiya Parivardhan Sanstha Vs Department of Social Welfare Page No 5/44 and it was always found that the additional inmates had gone beyond the sanctions capacity from the month of March 2012 onwards. xiv. That the month-wise additional inmates, starting from March 2012 till December 2012, assigned for drug de-addiction centre run by the plaintiff and the amount payable for additional inmates is hereby as follows:- Month (Year-2012) Additional inmates Amount payable for additional inmates March 13 4,130/- April 336 1,09,200/- Bhartiya Parivardhan Sanstha vs Department Of Social Welfare on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51433371/ 3 May 685 2,21,650/- June 595 1,93,050/- July 1050 3,41,240/- August 1339 4,35,139/- September 1508 4,90,035/- October 1702 5,53,117/- November 1635 5,14,215/- December 1265 4,11,125/- ---------- Total- 32,72,901/ xv. That the abovesaid amount has been calculated by the plaintiff at the rate of Rs. 325/- per additional inmate per day as per the formula laid down by the department for the calculation of expenditure on per inmate per day basis. CS No 14758/16 Bhartiya Parivardhan Sanstha Vs Department of Social Welfare Page No 6/44 xvi. That due to the intra departmental differences in the Department of Social Welfare between its Principal Secretary and Director, the rate of Rs. 325/- per additional inmate per day as spent by the plaintiff on actual basis was drastically reduced to Rs.119/- per inmate per day for the additional inmates in an arbitrary and whimsical manner. xvii. That the plaintiff through its Secretary had given representation to the Chief Secretary, Govt. of NCT of Delhi i.e. defendant no.5 and Principle Secretary, Department of Social Welfare, Govt. of NCT of Delhi regarding the financial problem the plaintiff had been facing for the upkeep and maintenance of the additional inmates being thrust upon the plaintiff by various beggar courts. xviii. That the Principle Secretary, Department of Social Welfare and Chief Secretary, Govt. of NCT of Delhi had concurred with the problems of the plaintiff and had even given written direction to the competent authority i.e.the Director, Social Welfare the defendant no.3 to immediately take over the running of the drug de-addiction centre at Lampur and make payment of legitimate dues to the plaintiff. xix. That the plaintiff was always harassed for its payments by asking for the details of cash memos/bills and the warrants for the additional inmates CS No 14758/16 Bhartiya Parivardhan Sanstha Vs Department of Social Welfare Page No 7/44 by the defendant no.3. Even after the detailed report having been given by the Superintendent, Beggars Home Lampur i.e. defendant No.3 and the other officials regarding the expenditure and the number of inmates, the defendant no.3 all the time sought more and more clarifications from the officials and every time she has been adequately briefed and all the bills and vouchers were shown to her but despite that she again put objections and sent the file for more clarifications leading to the delay the payments to the plaintiff. Bhartiya Parivardhan Sanstha vs Department Of Social Welfare on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51433371/ 4 xx. That the Principle Secretary, Department of Social Welfare had even reprimanded the defendant no.3 for acting in a prejudicial manner and targeting the plaintiff and had therefore constituted a committee headed by the Director (WCD) and two other members to examine the claim of the plaintiff. xxi. That the committee so constituted by the order of the Principle Secretary had examined in detail all the bills, vouchers, warrants and other essential documents and had given its report whereby the calculation as devised by the department of Social Welfare of Rs.319/- per inmates per day for additional inmates was approved by the committee and the department was asked to release the payments to the plaintiff. CS No 14758/16 Bhartiya Parivardhan Sanstha Vs Department of Social Welfare Page No 8/44 xxii. That despite that the defendant no.3 devised its own formula which was not there in the work order/contract and calculated the expenditure at Rs.119/- per inmates per day for each additional inmate and on that basis had given payment to the plaintiff for additional inmates for the period from March 2012 to December 2012. xxiii. That the plaintiff had claimed expenditure of Rs. 325/- per inmates per day for each additional inmates on an actual basis and therefore had claimed Rs. 32,72,901/- as outstanding dues payable to the plaintiff from March 2012 till 25th December 2012. The defendants, however had paid an amount of Rs. 11,96,995/- for additional inmates during the said period on the basis of the calculation as devised by the defendant no.3 leaving an outstanding of Rs. 20,75,906/- payable to the plaintiff by the defendants. xxiv. That the plaintiff had since 25th December 2012 handed over the running of the said Beggar complex at Lampur to the defendants with all its infrastructure and nothing remains on the part of the plaintiff to be handed over to the defendants. xxv. That the plaintiff had written to the defendants on a number of occasions for the settlement of dues and payment of its outstanding dues CS No 14758/16 Bhartiya Parivardhan Sanstha Vs Department of Social Welfare Page No 9/44 but so far the defendants have not paid anything of the remaining amount of Rs. 20,75,900/- to the plaintiff and the same remains to be paid. xxvi. That the plaintiff after having failed in all its endeavors to get back its outstanding dues from the defendants had no option but to send a legal notice dated 18.02.2014 by registered post through its lawyer to the defendants as per law asking them to make the payments within sixty days from the receipt of the legal notice but despite the service of the notice they failed to make the payments to the plaintiff. Thus the present suit and the plaintiff has sought following reliefs: a) Pass a decree in favour of plaintiff and against the defendants to the tune of Rs. 20,00,000/- (Rupees twenty lakhs only); b) Pass an order for an interest of 24% p.a. from the date of accrual to the realization; Bhartiya Parivardhan Sanstha vs Department Of Social Welfare on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51433371/ 5 c) Cost of the suit may also be awarded in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendant; d) Any other order/s or direction/s which this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper in facts and circumstances of the case. CS No 14758/16 Bhartiya Parivardhan Sanstha Vs Department of Social Welfare Page No 10/44 WRITTEN STATEMENT 2. The defendants were served with the summons of the suit on 22.08.2014 and has filed joint written statement on 23.09.2014 challenging the suit of the plaintiff pleading inter-alia as follows: a) That the present suit is not maintainable as it is gross abuse to the process of law. b) That the present suit is not maintainable as the plaintiff himself has violated the terms and conditions of the work order to run and maintain the drug de-addiction centre. c) The plaintiff has not come with clean hands and has concealed/suppressed material facts. On Merits, it is submitted that the proposal for running 20 bedded de- addiction centre was awarded to the plaintiff on the basis of bid document. It was admitted that the plaintiff was engaged to set up and run a newly created 20 bedded drug de-addiction centre initially for one year from November, 2010 to October, 2011 and thereafter extension was given till December, 2011. Perusal of the record shows that vide order dt 08.03.2022, Ld counsel for the plaintiff had submitted that the plaintiff is not pressing their suit qua defendant no 2 to 4. Separate statement of the Ld Counsel for the plaintiff has been recorded to this effect on the very same day and accordingly defendants no 2-4 stood deleted from the memo of parties and amended memo of parties was filed against the present defendants. The plaintiff, in order to prove his case, has examined 4 witnesses. F (OSR) Favourable notes written by the Director, Social Welfare in the visitors book of Centre obtained from the defendant by way of RTI 7 Ex PW1/G & Ex Copy of legal notice sent on behalf of the PW 1/H plaintiff to the defendant and postal receipt. 7. PW-1 was duly cross examined by Ld counsel for the defendants. 8. Thereafter, PW -2 Sh M Joseph, Senior Superintendent of Social Welfare, District Officer, North-East at: Sanskar Asshram, Dilshad Garden, Delhi was examined in chief, cross examined and discharged. Sh Krishan Kumar who was Deputy Director from Department of Social Welfare, Govt of NCT of Delhi was examined. He brought the official file pertaining to the Bhartiya Parivardhan Sanstha who have seen the photocopies of the official noting from judicial file from page No. 22 to 73 which formed part of the official file of the Department of Social Welfare except the document at page No. 64. The total number of pages are 52 which are already Ex.PW1/B (colly). 10. PW-4 Sh Ajay Arora who is the Deputy Director in Department of Social Welfare, Govt of NCT of Delhi, GLNS Complex, Delhi Gate, Delhi who brought the file pertaining to Bhartiya Parivardhan Sanstha and stated that he CS No 14758/16 Bhartiya Parivardhan Sanstha Vs Department of Social Welfare Page No 15/44 has seen document at page no 64 of the judicial file which forms part of the official file of the department and is already exhibited as PW 1/C (colly) in the official file at page no 131/N. 11. Thereafter, PE was closed on 20.07.2022. The defendant, in order to prove his case, has examined only one witness i.e. Sh Rajeev Saksena, Dy Director (SD), from the office of Social Welfare Department, Govt of NCT of Delhi, GLNS Complex, Delhi Gate, Delhi who entered into the witness box and tendered his affidavit by way of evidence as DW1/1. Thereafter Office of the Secretary (SW/WCD/GAD/Labour) Government of NCT of Delhi, in order to examine the claim of the NGO constituted a committee.
texts.arguments: It is further submitted that the plaintiff himself stopped the services of the drug de-addiction centre before the department can take over it due to which it resulted in great disservice to the inmates & creating CS No 14758/16 Bhartiya Parivardhan Sanstha Vs Department of Social Welfare Page No 11/44 admission difficulties for the department in the welfare activities in the said home. It is further submitted that as per the work order awarded to the plaintiff, the defendant undertook to provide free of cost building space, electricity, water facility to the partner NGO. It is further submitted that since there was no legal obligation on the part of the plaintiff to admit more inmates than the sanctioned capacity, no work order was placed by the department. It is further submitted that plaintiff had never sought permission in advance to keep more staff for additional inmates from the department in writing. It is further submitted that the amount released was to be in conformity with the numbers of inmates and consumed rate to the actual amount incurred on medicine/consumables/service provided which was accepted by the plaintiff and now the plaintiff is not adhering to the same. It is further submitted that the additional inmates was reported only from March 2012 onwards till December 2012. It is further submitted that the department had to calculate the rate for payment for additional inmates on per day per inmate basis and payment was released to the plaintiff for the period March,2012 to December, 2012 on the basis of the rate fixed by the department @ Rs. 119/- per inmate per day. It is thus submitted that the present suit be dismissed. The plaintiff filed his replication to the written statement filed by the defendant by denying the allegations levelled by the defendant and reiterating the contents of the plaint. The liability of the defendant to reimburse the plaintiff at the agreed rate as per the work order arises under the provisions of Section 70 of the Indian Contract Act which is reproduced herein below for ready reference: Obligation of person enjoying benefit of non gratuitous act--where a person lawfully does anything for another person, or delivers anything to him, not intending to do so gratuitously, and such other person enjoys the benefit thereof, the latter is bound to make compensation to the former in respect of, or to restore, the thing so done or delivered.
